### Arcata

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-09-16 (City Council, 5-0), Ordinance No. 1594
- **Normalized date:** `2026-09-16` (exact)
- **Duration:** 45-day interim urgency ordinance; extendable 10 months 15 days, then up to 12 more months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-arcata-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 1594 (Govt. Code 65858) moratorium on new data center land use applications
- **What prompted it:** No zoning definition for data centers; concern over scarce industrial land/resources; recent reports of a proposed 30,000-50,000 sq ft facility locally; existing small EdgeConneX colocation facility unaffected.
- **Affected projects:** Existing 10,000 sq ft EdgeConneX colocation facility (fiber terminal) is legally permitted/operating and unaffected.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Adopted 5-0 on 2026-09-16, effective immediately for 45 days; staff to report back by Oct. 21 (day 35).
- **Outcome:** Staff evaluating land-use definitions, environmental impacts, infrastructure capacity, and regulatory models.

### Coachella

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-04 (Coachella City Council special meeting approved an interim urgency moratorium on data centers, per NBC Palm Springs and kvcrnews.org reporting); extended on or about 2026-07-09 while the city drafts a permanent ban
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-04` (exact)
- **Duration:** Consistent with the Gov. Code section 65858 interim urgency ordinance pattern already documented elsewhere in this inventory (initial up to 45 days, extendable to a 2-year maximum by 4/5 vote): reported as an initial temporary/urgency moratorium adopted 2026-06-04, then extended around 2026-07-09 ('Coachella Extends Temporary Ban On Data Center Developments,' Patch) as the council moves toward a permanent ban. Exact day counts and vote margins were not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
- **Current end date:** `2026-09-25`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-coachella-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 1229 (adopted 2026-06-04, 45-day pause); extended by Urgency Ordinance No. 1230 (adopted 2026-07-08/09, 10 months 15 days); superseded by Ordinance No. 1231, adding Chapter 17.92 to the Coachella Municipal Code to permanently prohibit data center uses citywide (first reading 2026-08-12, second reading/adoption 2026-08-26, effective 30 days after adoption).
- **What prompted it:** Public backlash and protests over a large proposed data center project and a power agreement with developer 'Stronghold'; council terminated the specific project and moved toward a permanent ban
- **Affected projects:** A large proposed data center project tied to a power agreement with 'Stronghold'; project reported terminated by the city (per NBC Palm Springs, 'Coachella City Council Halts Data Center Project, Cuts Ties with Stronghold,' 2026-06-05)
- **Detailed status:** Replaced as of 2026-09-23. The City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1231 on 2026-08-26 (second reading), permanently prohibiting data center uses citywide (with limited exceptions for accessory server/IT rooms); effective 2026-09-25, thirty days after adoption. Mayor Figueroa has also voiced support for a future ballot measure to entrench the ban, but no such measure had been placed on a ballot as of this pass.
- **Outcome:** Moratorium adopted (Ord. 1229) and extended 10 months 15 days (Ord. 1230); superseded by a permanent citywide prohibition on data centers (Ord. 1231), adopted 2026-08-26 and effective 2026-09-25. Coachella is the first Coachella Valley city and second California city (after Monterey Park) to permanently ban data centers.

### Imperial

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-03 (City Council unanimous adoption of Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 834, per meeting summary and a contemporaneous Coachella staff report survey of nearby municipal actions)

Contrary to the prior 'expired' classification, the City Council held a public hearing 2026-07-15 and unanimously (5-0) adopted Urgency Ordinance No. 835, extending Ordinance No. 834 for up to 10 months and 15 days under Gov. Code section 65858, so that -- as multiple sources independently confirm -- the City of Imperial's pause on data centers, high-performance computing facilities, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) runs through approximately May 2027. This remains a distinct instrument and jurisdiction from the Imperial County Board of Supervisors' moratorium (ca-imperial-county-2026, since rescinded by court order), which covers unincorporated county land, not the City of Imperial.

- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-imperial-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 834, adopted under California Gov. Code section 65858
- **What prompted it:** Pause on approvals for data centers, battery energy storage systems, and similar utility-intensive industrial/technology uses while the city studies zoning and development standards
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Active/extended as of 2026-09-23 -- correcting the prior 'expired' classification. Following a July 15, 2026 public hearing, the City Council unanimously (5-0) adopted Urgency Ordinance No. 835, extending Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 834 by up to 10 months and 15 days (to approximately 2027-05-30/through May 2027), continuing the pause on data centers, high-performance computing facilities, and battery energy storage systems (BESS) citywide while staff finishes defining data-center categories, mapping feasible industrial sites, and evaluating environmental and labor impacts. KPBS ('the city of Imperial has also temporarily frozen all data center development through May 2027') and Hoodline both independently confirm this as of August 2026, and no further change was found through 2026-09-23. This is unrelated to, and unaffected by, the Imperial County Superior Court's September 2026 order setting aside the separate Imperial County Board of Supervisors moratorium (ca-imperial-county-2026), which governs unincorporated county land only.
- **Outcome:** —

### Imperial County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🔴 Rescinded
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-17
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-17` (exact)
- **Duration:** Extended to a one-year moratorium on 2026-07-14; reported to run into June 2027 while the County's advisory committee develops recommendations.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-imperial-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** County Ordinance No. 1616 (adopted 2026-06-16, initial 45-day moratorium) and County Ordinance No. 1618 (adopted 2026-07-14, extension of ~10 months 15 days); both ordinances were set aside by court order effective 2026-09-11 (see current_status).
- **What prompted it:** Months of public opposition to a large proposed data center complex projected to consume about 750,000 gallons of water daily and more electricity than the entire county used in 2024
- **Affected projects:** A proposed large-scale data center complex; the developer (reported as Sebastian Rucci) indicated plans to challenge the decision in court.
- **Detailed status:** Rescinded by court order as of 2026-09-23. Imperial County Superior Court Judge Jeffrey B. Jones entered judgment 2026-09-04 in favor of developer Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC, finding neither Ordinance 1616 (the original moratorium) nor Ordinance 1618 (its ~10-month-15-day extension) made the causal finding of a 'current and immediate threat to public health, safety, or welfare' required by Gov. Code section 65858. A peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 directs the County and Board of Supervisors to set aside both ordinances and stop using them to withhold, suspend, or refuse data-center permits. The County has said (per KYMA, 2026-09-22) it is working on a new moratorium addressing the court's concerns; no replacement had been adopted as of 2026-09-23. The Data Center Advisory Committee, created alongside the moratorium, continues to meet (inaugural meeting 2026-09-17) and is unaffected by the ruling. Separately, a different judge (L. Brooks Anderholt) has ordered a full CEQA environmental review of the underlying data center project in a related case, so the project itself remains stalled notwithstanding the moratorium's invalidation.
- **Outcome:** Moratorium (Ordinances 1616 and 1618) adopted and extended to run through mid-2027, then invalidated by the Imperial County Superior Court (Judge Jeffrey B. Jones) in Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC v. County of Imperial: judgment entered 2026-09-04, peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 ordering the County to set aside and cease enforcing both ordinances because their findings did not satisfy Gov. Code section 65858's 'current and immediate threat' standard. The County has 30 days after service of the writ to file a return; county officials say they are preparing a new moratorium that addresses the court's findings. The Data Center Advisory Committee process continues separately.

### Los Angeles County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active

- **Normalized date:** `2026-09-17` (exact)
- **Duration:** Interim administrative prohibition on processing/approving large-scale (hyperscale) AI data centers in unincorporated county zones, in effect until the Board of Supervisors adopts a permanent zoning ordinance. A motion to formally initiate that ordinance was scheduled for a Community Services Cluster Agenda Review on 2026-09-23, with a Board of Supervisors hearing expected around 2026-10-06.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-los-angeles-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Department of Regional Planning Director's memorandum (interim planning guidance), issued pursuant to and implementing the Board of Supervisors' unanimous April 14, 2026 motion (Solis) directing staff to study and recommend data-center zoning code amendments; a formal ordinance was in preparation as of this pass, not yet adopted by the Board.
- **What prompted it:** San Gabriel Valley community concerns over health, environmental, water, and electricity impacts of hyperscale AI data centers (following the Monterey Park/SDCF controversy and other regional moratoria); Board of Supervisors motion directing a zoning study; noise, air-quality, and utility-rate concerns cited by county Public Health and Public Works directors.
- **Affected projects:** No hyperscale data centers currently sited in unincorporated county areas as of the memo; about 74 data centers operate elsewhere within LA County (mostly in incorporated cities), unaffected by the county action.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. On Sept. 17, 2026, LA County's Department of Regional Planning director issued a memorandum imposing an immediate, interim prohibition on new hyperscale AI data center development in all zones of unincorporated county territory (about 1 million of the county's 10 million residents), pending Board of Supervisors adoption of a formal ordinance. A motion to formally initiate that ordinance was on the agenda for a Sept. 23, 2026 Community Services Cluster Agenda Review meeting, with Board consideration expected around Oct. 6, 2026. Smaller enterprise/accessory/sole-source data centers are not covered by the prohibition.
- **Outcome:** Interim administrative ban imposed via Regional Planning Director memorandum while the Board of Supervisors moves to adopt a permanent zoning ordinance banning hyperscale AI data centers in unincorporated areas.

### Monterey Park

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2026-01-21; extended 2026-03-04
- **Normalized date:** `2026-01-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** Initial 45 days; extended 10 months and 15 days; expires 2027-01-21 unless changed
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ca-monterey-park-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 2272; extension Ordinance No. 2274; Gov. Code sections 36937 and 65858
- **What prompted it:** 1977 Saturn Street data center proposal and broader concern over energy use, noise, air quality, aesthetics, property values, neighborhood quality of life, CEQA review, and whether permanent regulations or a citywide ban are needed
- **Affected projects:** 1977 Saturn Street proposal by HMC StratCap (SheppardMullin counsel); local CEQA/project records described about 49.9 MW maximum load, 36 MW critical load, 14 backup diesel generators, and roughly 218,400 to 247,480 sq ft in different documents. Per *San Gabriel Valley Tribune* (2026-04-01), HMC StratCap formally withdrew the Saturn Street application after community pushback; city officials confirmed on 2026-04-20 that HMC StratCap still owns the parcel and has not communicated future plans for the site.
- **Detailed status:** Active; permanent citywide data center prohibition in place. Measure NDC passed at the June 2, 2026 special election (10,388 Yes / 1,372 No, per the LA County Registrar-Recorder's certified canvass); results certified by the City Clerk on June 30, 2026 and declared by City Council Resolution No. 2026-R56 on July 1, 2026 (unanimous, 5-0). Companion Ordinance No. 2280 (General Plan amendment prohibiting all data centers citywide) was adopted by Council on July 2, 2026, effective on or about July 11, 2026 (10 days after election-result certification, per Elections Code section 9217).
- **Outcome:** Moratorium extended through 2027-01-21 (superseded in practice by permanent action); permanent citywide prohibition codified by ordinance on 2026-04-20; voters ratified the prohibition via Measure NDC on 2026-06-02 (10,388 Yes / 1,372 No), with results certified July 1, 2026 and companion Ordinance No. 2280 adopted July 2, 2026.
